Prevention: Avoid planting in fields with known history of cutworm problems
Weed 2 weeks before planting; Brush around the field about 10 to 20 metres away
Monitoring: Observe for the presence of the eggs on the leaves and larvae at the base of the plant or underneath debris
Monitor for young larvae that may have clipped very near or just below the soil surface
Dig soil to confirm the presence of cutworm larvae
When the soil is moist, the cutworm caterpillars cut the plant just above the soil surface
When soil is dry, cutworms will feed on the plant just below the soil surface, causing the plant to wilt and die
Direct Control: Hand pick adults and eggs on leaves
Dig soil to expose larvae to predators such as birds and ants
Restrictions: Apply insecticides to the ground around affected plants; Always ensure your protective gears / apparels are put on, e.g. goggles, overalls, etc.
III (Slightly hazardous); Once sprayed, cutworms get sick the first day after application and then die
